content:
**The five rock bands that rank highest in worldwide album‑sales (according to the Wikipedia “List of biggest‑selling British music artists” and related sales tables) are:**

| Rank (by claimed album sales) | Band | Approx. claimed album sales* | Lead vocalist(s) |
|------------------------------|------|-----------------------------|------------------|
| 1 | **The Beatles** | ~600 million | **John Lennon** and **Paul McCartney** (both shared lead‑vocal duties; George Harrison and Ringo Starr also sang lead on several tracks) |
| 2 | **The Rolling Stones** | ~200 million | **Mick Jagger** |
| 3 | **Led Zeppelin** | 200‑300 million | **Robert Plant** |
| 4 | **Pink Floyd** | ~200 million | **David Gilmour** (took over lead vocals after Syd Barrett’s departure) |
| 5 | **Queen** | 170‑200 million | **Freddie Mercury** |

\*These figures are the “claimed sales” numbers listed in the Wikipedia tables for the respective artists.  

**Sources**

* **The Beatles** – “600 million” sales listed under the “400 million or more records” section of *List of biggest‑selling British music artists*【...fragment 5】.  
* **The Rolling Stones** – “200 million” sales shown in the same table【...fragment 4】.  
* **Led Zeppelin** – “200‑300 million” sales shown in the “300 million to 400 million records” section【...fragment 5】.  
* **Pink Floyd** – “200 million” sales listed in the “200 million to 299 million records” section【...fragment 4】.  
* **Queen** – “170‑200 million” sales listed in the “200 million to 299 million records” section【...fragment 4】.  

**Why these vocalists are considered the “lead” singers**

* **The Beatles** – Lennon and McCartney wrote and sang the bulk of the group’s material; they are universally recognised as the band’s primary vocalists.  
* **The Rolling Stones** – Mick Jagger has been the front‑man and principal vocalist since the group’s formation.  
* **Led Zeppelin** – Robert Plant’s distinctive high‑range voice is the defining vocal element on virtually all of the band’s studio recordings.  
* **Pink Floyd** – After Syd Barrett left, David Gilmour assumed lead‑vocal duties on the majority of the band’s later albums.  
* **Queen** – Freddie Mercury’s powerful, operatic voice was the unmistakable lead on virtually every Queen track.

These five acts together account for well over a billion album sales and remain the most commercially successful rock groups in history.

**The five rock bands that rank highest in worldwide album‑sales (according to the Wikipedia “List of biggest‑selling British music artists” and related sales tables) are:**

| Rank (by claimed album sales) | Band | Approx. claimed album sales* | Lead vocalist(s) |
|------------------------------|------|-----------------------------|------------------|
| 1 | **The Beatles** | ~600 million | **John Lennon** and **Paul McCartney** (both shared lead‑vocal duties; George Harrison and Ringo Starr also sang lead on several tracks) |
| 2 | **The Rolling Stones** | ~200 million | **Mick Jagger** |
| 3 | **Led Zeppelin** | 200‑300 million | **Robert Plant** |
| 4 | **Pink Floyd** | ~200 million | **David Gilmour** (took over lead vocals after Syd Barrett’s departure) |
| 5 | **Queen** | 170‑200 million | **Freddie Mercury** |

\*These figures are the “claimed sales” numbers listed in the Wikipedia tables for the respective artists.  

**Sources**

* **The Beatles** – “600 million” sales listed under the “400 million or more records” section of *List of biggest‑selling British music artists*【...fragment 5】.  
* **The Rolling Stones** – “200 million” sales shown in the same table【...fragment 4】.  
* **Led Zeppelin** – “200‑300 million” sales shown in the “300 million to 400 million records” section【...fragment 5】.  
* **Pink Floyd** – “200 million” sales listed in the “200 million to 299 million records” section【...fragment 4】.  
* **Queen** – “170‑200 million” sales listed in the “200 million to 299 million records” section【...fragment 4】.  

**Why these vocalists are considered the “lead” singers**

* **The Beatles** – Lennon and McCartney wrote and sang the bulk of the group’s material; they are universally recognised as the band’s primary vocalists.  
* **The Rolling Stones** – Mick Jagger has been the front‑man and principal vocalist since the group’s formation.  
* **Led Zeppelin** – Robert Plant’s distinctive high‑range voice is the defining vocal element on virtually all of the band’s studio recordings.  
* **Pink Floyd** – After Syd Barrett left, David Gilmour assumed lead‑vocal duties on the majority of the band’s later albums.  
* **Queen** – Freddie Mercury’s powerful, operatic voice was the unmistakable lead on virtually every Queen track.

These five acts together account for well over a billion album sales and remain the most commercially successful rock groups in history.
